notes.title: A Huge Thank You!
notes.notes:
[u][b]One Month After the Expansion[/b][/u]
It’s been a month since the expansion launched, and with it, our celebration event has came to an end.

We crafted this expansion as a way to give more to all the great players who have supported the game since its release. We worked hard, without huge expectations. 
Well, it backfired in the best possible way, as the expansion's release was a much bigger success than we anticipated.

Thousands of you picked up the game last month, and on January 12th, [b]1,610 players were online in a single day[/b] - a new record, even surpassing our original launch!

Reading your feedback has been a highlight of this journey. Your words of support for the game have meant the world to us. Thank you for playing, and thank you for sharing your experiences with us. It makes all the work truly worthwhile. 
[img]https://i.imgur.com/N240ae1.png[/img]

[u][b]Expansion Challenges – Final Results[/b][/u]
The challenges are now officially over! 120+ players have earned a place on the Expansion Eternal Wall, and in the second challenge, the Order side emerged victorious. More details on the event location and the Order’s world event can be found here: [url=https://svarogsdream.wiki.gg/wiki/Expansion_Release_-_Special_Event]link[/url]
Congratulations to everyone who participated!

As a bonus celebration, we’ve also added two new hand-drawn animated Svarog's Dream [url=https://store.steampowered.com/points/shop/app/2004640]stickers[/url] to the Steam.


[img]https://i.imgur.com/IlFTX7V.jpeg[/img]

[u][b]Looking Ahead[/b][/u]
With the expansion wrapped up, we’ll be taking some time off during spring and summer to rest and focus on life-related matters.
We’ll still provide support and release smaller updates if necessary, but things won’t be as fast-paced as they were for the past month. 

As for the new projects, there are plenty of ideas written down—some even for a completely different kind of game. But for now, nothing is set in motion. We won’t start working on anything until winter, and we won’t discuss future plans until we’ve had time to explore what works, what doesn’t, and until we see where life takes us.

Once again, thank you so much! 
I hope this game brought something positive to your life, or at least that you had an enjoyable time playing it.

notes.title: Making death a bit more interesting
notes.notes:
If you're not fully familiar with how death works in this game, you can read more about it on the [url=https://svarogsdream.wiki.gg/wiki/Death]wiki[/url].
Some players love the reincarnation system, while others aren’t big fans. This update aims to make it more enjoyable for everyone by improving the fun parts and cutting the frustrating bits.

[b]Patch v6.5.2[/b] – What’s New?

[b]Character Rerolls[/b] – 
After death, you can now reroll your next character for 3 God’s Favors.
You can keep rerolling as long as you have God's Favors to spend or until you find the chosen one.
[b]12 New Characters[/b] – 
Each comes with a unique (Expertise) talent, only obtainable through resurrection.
These new talents are designed to shake up different playstyles and can only be acquired by finding the right characters in a much larger pool of those with common traits.
[b]Gender[/b] – 
If two characters of the same gender appear, the third will be the opposite.
[b]Consequences[/b] -
After dying too many times, the consequences on the world will become more visible than before.

There are a few more tweaks and game updates, check the full details in this [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/2004640/discussions/0/599644333221643172/]thread[/url].

The idea here is to give you more control over who you play after death, and maybe even leave you more excited to continue than before you died.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/fo7GMec.png[/img]

[b]One of the Last Major Updates Before Our Break[/b]
We’ll be taking a longer break soon, but before that, this Saturday, we’ll be posting expansion release challenge results and our reflections on January. Stay tuned!

notes.title: Patch v6.4.0 – Major Class Balance Update and More
notes.notes:
[b]Class Skill Updates[/b]
We’ve reviewed player feedback from both veterans and newcomers to identify class imbalances.

As you probably know, in the game, you can mix up to four classes from the 15 available. The question isn’t just about which class is strong on its own, but rather which ones are worth committing to in order to find skills that synergize with others from different classes.

With this in mind, our goal with the patch was not simply to buff some numbers, we actually added new skills to struggling classes to make them more interesting.

Among around 30 class updates, we are [b]introducing 12 new passive skills and 1 new active skill[/b].

Fire and Ice mages received the most attention as they really struggled in mid-to-late-game, but 14 out of 15 classes received some updates. Full details and our reasoning can be found in the thread [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/2004640/discussions/0/591762021826965009/]here[/url].

[b]Achievements Rework[/b]
Most achievements can now be earned outside of Ironman mode.
Why? A part of playerbase felt restricted by Ironman-only achievements, so we made a compromise:
- 86 achievements are now available in all modes, including one for reaching any ending.
- 5 achievements remain exclusive to Ironman for reaching all five endings on ironman.

For 100% completionists, the challenge remains almost as difficult as before, but now all players can feel rewarded.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/Q8ZJKin.jpeg[/img]

[b]Item Updates[/b]
Underperforming items received buffs, there are new options for lifesteal.
Item Critical chance now scales with weapon quality to make it more attractive.

[b]Clarity Improvements[/b]
20+ passive skills that require specific conditions (e.g., night-based or weapon-based) now display buff icons when full condition is met.
This way, if you're unsure whether a poleaxe counts for spear or axe buffs, you can always check the buff icon in the lower right corner.

[b]Fixes & Optimizations[/b]
Since the expansion’s release, we've pushed 120+ updates, including bug fixes, QoL changes, and performance improvements.  
We are at a point where all reported major issues have been resolved, and we are now primarily addressing low-priority issues and some QoL requests.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/nL42Z4v.jpeg[/img]

notes.title: Expansion Preview #6: New Story and Celestial Battles
notes.notes:
We invested four years of work into the core game, which features four endings. 
Symbolically, our fifth year of development brings an expansion, and with it, a [b]fifth ending[/b].

[b]Expansion Story[/b]
In the original game, the old gods remained fractured, without a unified path. The expansion seeks to change that. Our main goal was to create a narrative where the old gods stand united, and we've built an entirely new questline to make it happen.

At the heart of this story is Stribog, the god of wind. His mission is monumental: to unite the old gods, rebuild the shattered Pantheon of Oak, and mount a true challenge against the new one-God.
Will he succeed? That’s up to you.

[b]Expansion Celestial Battles[/b]
To reflect the expansion’s bold themes, we’ve reimagined the boss fights.
Players will now face celestial foes: actual angels.

Prepare to battle three epic bosses inspired by biblical lore: Seraphim, Thrones, and Cherubim.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/tDJsF20.jpeg[/img]

Developer side note: [i]We understand that introducing biblical beings into our stories may not resonate with everyone. However, we want to emphasize that this is a fantasy game. Borrowing themes from religious mythology allows us to explore deeper ideas within the narrative, something we've done since the beginning of Svarog's Dream.[/i]

With that being said, let's return to gameplay. 
As with the core game, our boss fights aim to deliver epic, unforgettable moments. 
Each major enemy features a unique musical theme, with their actions synchronized to the audio theme. Here's a sneak peek:

https://youtu.be/RwOitB886Fc

In addition to the main story bosses, the expansion includes optional side bosses, demigods waiting to challenge you. Their stories and battles are left for you to discover.

[b]Becoming a Demigod[/b]
In a recent preview, a player asked if it was possible to become a demigod. Initially, we hadn't planned for it, but the idea struck a chord with us. So, we made it happen.
Yes, you can now ascend to become a demigod, though exactly how remains for you to uncover.

This expansion is not just our creation, it’s a product of the incredible ideas, feedback, and support from you, the players. Many of the features you’ll experience came directly from your suggestions.

Thank you for being part of this journey and for helping us bring this world to life. We can’t wait for you to explore what we’ve built.

The expansion launches in just 2 days, on [b]January 9th[/b]! 
To celebrate, we’ve prepared a special event. See you in two days when we reveal it!

notes.title: Expansion Preview #5: Two New Classes and some Lore
notes.notes:
Hello! There are less than two weeks until the expansion's release. 
In today's article, we will introduce two new classes debuting with the expansion.

[b]Beastbane[/b]
The Beastbane is a melee, order-oriented class that scales with the number of beasts you've hunted.
This class unlocks the ability to wield two melee weapons, a feature that has been highly requested by players in the past.
[b]Dual-wielding[/b] weapons simultaneously applies the buffs of both, making the class as strong as the quality of gear you can find. This ability is balanced by the significant number of points required to fully unlock it.
If you enjoy investing heavily in passive skills and tearing through enemies with auto-attacks rather than relying on active abilities, this class is perfect for you.

[b]Doombringer[/b]
The Doombringer is a chaos-oriented support class that is not dependent on any specific weapon.
Designed to be chaotic and counterintuitive, it’s a unique choice for those looking to experiment with something different. Its skills scale with the number of negative talents you possess, as well as with the newly introduced cursed gear.
Notable abilities include an AOE skill that charms enemies, turning them against one another and cursed eyes that grow stronger with time. 
The class also offers a range of supportive skills, such as the ability to summon a container on demand to store loot, etc.

Both classes are showcased in this video: https://youtu.be/8ZiASLtiUSA

*****************************************************

As the year turns and the cold deepens, we look to [b]Morana[/b], the goddess of winter and death.

[i]In the actual mythology, Morana was not well-loved by worshippers, leaving few preserved stories about her. In some regions, her tales were even conflated with those of Mokosh, blurring the lines between them. 
One ritual tied to Morana has survived: a doll of straw, made in her image, is beaten, drowned, and burned to drive her away and shorten winter's hold.[/i]
[img]https://i.imgur.com/swIa1SU.png[/img]

The Game’s Lore:
[i]In Svarog's Dream, Morana plays a central role, guiding souls to Veles in the underworld. 

One tale tells of a village built around her shrine, where a powerful magician-priest rose to the status of a demigod, turned to other gods, and even dared to challenge Morana to a duel. 
The battle ended in devastation, Morana obliterated the village and froze an entire region in eternal winter. The priest survived, though his body was shattered, forcing him to craft a mask and robe to conceal his ruined form.
You can find this priest in the southeastern parts of the map, where he is known as the Priest Guardian.[/i]

*****************************************************

That’s all for this preview article. 
Happy New Year, happy holidays, and we’ll see you next year!

notes.title: Expansion Preview #4: Faction Wars and Other Updates
notes.notes:
The release of our expansion is just three weeks away! This is the fourth article in our series about what the expansion brings, and this time, we will talk more about the new side content added to the game.

[b]Faction Wars[/b]
The core game already featured faction wars as part of the main story, but they were limited in terms of which factions you could join and what territories you could conquer.
With the expansion, we’ve split the world into 16 areas, each controlled by one of six different factions.
As a player, you can now join any of these six factions and work to paint the whole world in their colors.

Conquering an area under your faction’s banner will replace the local citizens, introduce unique NPCs, and trigger related world events.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/8g7vTa5.jpeg[/img]

To conquer a territory, you’ll need to initiate a siege and assist your army, much like in the core game.
This content will be available as a late game side quests, which unlock either after completing the war portion of the main story or upon reaching a certain point in the expansion’s alternate main storyline.

Playable factions include House of Faith, House of Coin, Free People, Underworld Horde, Devourers (new) and Lizards (new).

A significant aspect of the game lies in the choices you make in the godly realm and the earthly realm, and how these two intertwine. With the Faction Wars update, we aim to make choices in the earthly realm more impactful.

Now, let's talk about a few other smaller updates that are related to crime and companions.

[b]Mercenaries[/b]
You can now purchase slaves to make them companions and assign them tasks, such as following you, guarding your home, or granting them their freedom.
Companions can be equipped with any gear you provide. However, don't expect them to be very intelligent, as they function as standard followers. They are designed as a small side addition to the gameplay.

[b]Head Hunt Quests[/b]
These optional side quests allow you to take contracts from bounty boards in villages. The more difficult the target, the higher the reward.
Some contracts might lead to crime-related troubles with villages, which ties into the last new mechanic we will discuss today.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/srrx4qe.jpeg[/img]
[b]Serving Crime Sentences[/b]
Previously, committing a crime (eg. stealing) meant you either paid your bounty or fought back, often escalating your troubles. Now, you can choose to serve your sentence to clear your record and regain your freedom.
We’re considering adding this feature to the core game in the future, as it feels like a natural fit.

*******************************************

That’s all for this content reveal article! 
Stay tuned for our next update, where we’ll showcase the two new classes coming to the game.

notes.title: Expansion Preview #3: New Items, Traders, and some Lore
notes.notes:
Here’s a smaller update on some additional content coming in the expansion.
Among other things, the expansion will expand the item pool with over 120 new unique items.

[b]New Items[/b]
We are introducing a new category of items known as [b]Cursed Items[/b]. 
These are weapons and gear with attributes often surpassing those of divine equipment but balanced by unique drawbacks. Over 40 Cursed Items will be unlocked with expansion.
Additionally, we are adding more than 20 new [b]offhand items[/b], offering offensive options for players wielding one-handed weapons instead of shields.
The expansion will also include new food and alchemy ingredients, fresh herbs, and an array of new recipes for food and potions crafted from these resources.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/LSysvMd.jpeg[/img]
[b]More Roaming Traders [/b]
We're adding more roaming traders who sell rare items and roaming attribute trainers, making the world feel more alive. These characters will travel between towns, and you may stumble upon them randomly.

[b]Caravan Protection[/b]
When talking about traders, we’ve also added a few side quests to protect traveling trader carts or simply pay a cart driver to travel across the map.
These quests aren’t very in-depth, but we thought they’d be a cool way to travel the map quickly if you’re not a fan of fast travel.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/oW1uW7T.jpeg[/img]

************************************************************************

We will continue with our lore posts, and this week we will mention:
[b]Mokosh[/b], the goddess of Water and Fertility, she is also associated with the Moon, Fate, and the protection of women.
In some descriptions, she is portrayed as an ugly woman made from the bodies of dead animals, who uses her charm to make others see her as a beautiful woman, while in others, she is simply a beautiful woman. It was believed that her sacred day was Friday, and women were expected to honor her by refraining from work on that day.

In one interesting myth, Mokosh had a son with Perun named Yarilo. 
Yarilo was stolen by Veles and taken to the underworld, where he spent his childhood. 
Once he grew up, he traveled from the Underworld to the Sky, passing through Earth and bringing Spring in the process. Perun, angered by Yarilo's upbringing under Veles, rejected him and smote him with lightning. 
However, Veles resurrected him, and the cycle repeated, bringing spring to the Earth each year.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/A4LAs64.png[/img]
************************************************************************

Soon, more posts are coming. 
Stay tuned to hear about new classes, areas, quests, and other new mechanics.

notes.title: Expansion Preview #2: Devotion, Shrines, and World Events
notes.notes:
Welcome to the second of seven posts where we’ll be diving into all the new features coming with the expansion. In this update, we’ll explore how we’re introducing more combat opportunities and making the world feel a bit more interactive.

[b]Devotion Shrines[/b] 
Scattered across the world, you’ll now find around 30 large and 60 small Devotion Shrines. These shrines are guarded by enemies, and cleansing them offers you the chance to devote them to [b]Order[/b] or [b]Chaos[/b].
Large shrines can also be dedicated to specific gods, unlocking skill [b]upgrades[/b] as a reward.

Our design philosophy for these shrines was to provide optional combat challenges throughout the game. Since death carries significant consequences, we’ve been cautious about overwhelming players with overly strong encounters in the open world. With these shrines, you can face tougher enemies on your own terms.

We’ve already showcased how all 12 core game classes interact with some of these shrines during the combat update patch. Check out the gameplay video here:  https://youtu.be/JIxfxJ6nBeg?si=dtxF3mKWcfOoJU96

[b]Devotion to Gods[/b]
The expansion brings a new character page where you can team up with one of the gods. Picking a deity means they’ll step in to help you now and then, each in their own unique way.

These divine interventions have long cooldowns, but how often they happen depends on your relationship with the god you’ve chosen. Your bond with them changes based on what you do in the game, the gods are always watching and judging how well your actions match their ideals.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/5Iqsfw9.png[/img]

[b]Order and Chaos Events[/b]
To make the balance between Order and Chaos more impactful, we’re adding over [b]60 new world events[/b]. These events will trigger based on the current state of the world:
-A world leaning toward Order will result in calmer gameplay.
-A world dominated by Chaos will bring more combat-heavy scenarios.

The idea behind the events is the same as before: to keep the world alive and interactive. We’re just doubling down on what you already enjoyed.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/WAXqpPt.jpeg[/img]

That’s all for this update! Stay tuned, there are five more posts coming your way as we unveil more about the expansion. See you in the next one!

notes.title: Expansion Preview #1: Fishing, Gardening, and Some Lore
notes.notes:
[b]Only Two Months Until the Expansion Release.[/b]
While you wait, we'll be sharing more about the new mechanics and content in a series of posts. 
This is the first of seven posts, so stay tuned for more!

[b]New Mechanic: Fishing[/b]
To start fishing, simply equip a fishing rod and cast it toward any water surface. 
Each fishing spot has a unique loot pool, with rewards ranging from common fish to divine treasures. 
There are even new exclusive items that can only be obtained by fishing.
The expansion will introduce different types of fishing rods, special rings to enhance fishing,
and a new attribute to increase your chances of finding the best loot quickly. 

Our goal with mechanics like this is to further enhance the meditative exploration aspect of the game, inviting you to check every lake and river as you journey through each area.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/tS6vNP3.jpeg[/img]

[b]New Mechanic: Gardening[/b]
The expansion also unlocks gardening, allowing you to cultivate your own plants. 
Each time you plant, you'll harvest an alchemical herb or cooking ingredient the next day. Different houses in various regions will yield unique plants.

For those who’ve already gathered most of the plants in the world, this feature provides an endless source of herbs and ingredients, plus, once a full in-game year passes, there is a new world event which will refresh plant life across the world.

************************************************************************

Since you enjoyed our post sharing lore about one of the gods, we'll continue with more! 
This week, we'll talk about:

[b]Veles, the God of the Underworld[/b]
[i]Some stories call him the protector of cattle, others say he’s the god of the underworld, and in certain places, he’s even linked to the sun or known as a trickster who looks out for musicians.
In ancient times, having a god protect your cattle was a big deal since a good herd could mean the difference between surviving winter or not. [/i]
In the game, we mention these different roles, but he’s mostly known as the god of the underworld.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/1SWeZ5N.jpeg[/img]

[i]In old tales, Veles and Perun, the thunder god, are famous for their clashes. 
Veles would steal Perun’s cattle, his wife, or even his children just to provoke him. This would lead to fierce battles. 
People believed these fights caused dry spells on Earth (when Veles stole from Perun), followed by storms and lightning (as they fought), and then rain when Perun got what was stolen back. 
Perun always won, but Veles’s defeat was never permanent - he’d keep coming back from the underworld.[/i]

In the game, Veles works alongside Perun against their common foe, but there are hints about their past conflicts, and some endings might even spark a new fight between them.

Veles is one of the key characters in the game. He’s the one who pulls you out of the underworld. 
And in the upcoming expansion, you’ll find out that he and Stribog have set up a whole new path for you to follow. 

Soon, more lore is coming.

************************************************************************

notes.title: How big is Svarog's Dream compared to Skyrim?
notes.notes:
We have received a few questions about how much content players should expect from this game, and we thought one way to answer and give you some perspective is by using Skyrim as a reference.

Why Skyrim? Because it is probably the most popular single-player open-world RPG ever to exist, and there is a good chance you have played it.

We are comparing both games on release, without any mods or expansions.

How large is the world?
Svarog's Dream: 20.2 Kilometers
Skyrim:  37 Kilometers
How many quests are there in the game?
Svarog's Dream: 126
Skyrim:  273
How many music compositions does the game use?
Svarog's Dream: 62 (about 3 hours)
Skyrim:  52 (about 4 hours)
How many lines are there in the game dialogues?
Svarog's Dream*: About 6.000 lines of dialogue or about 45.000 words
Skyrim:  About 60.000 lines of dialogue

*The dialogue in Svarog's Dream is not voiced.

Some other numbers about Svarog's Dream on release: 
Playable characters: 50
Active skills: 84
Unique talents: 58
Unique items: 560
World events: 46
Unique plants: 30
Plants to gather: 3768
Game endings: 4 (3 of them can lead to NG+)

The number of words in all the text in the game is about 80,000, which is roughly equivalent to the word count of an average novel of 300 pages.

When it comes to quest length, it really varies—from quests that took us only 1 hour to implement (e.g., learn how to cook food) to quests that took us weeks to create (e.g., God of War with a whole area made for that quest).

If there are any other numbers you would like to learn about the game, feel free to ask in the comments.
Also, we are curious to hear more about how many hours you spent in the game so far.

notes.title: Talking about the Future
notes.notes:
Starting from January, we will take a longer period of time to rest. 
We have worked on this game for four years and provided support to players after the release, and now it is time to refill our energy. Don't expect new updates in the first part of 2024.

[b]What comes after that?[/b]

The game received so much love and positive feedback from players, which has made us want to make an expansion to the core game. 

The expansion would have two main goals:
[b]1. To give more love to the Old Gods. [/b]
They are imagined to be morally ambiguous, like nature, and while nature can be cruel, it can also be beautiful. 
We would love to expand more on that positive side of Old Gods, with new quests, new main story quest paths, additional game endings, and more unique interactions with the Old Godss.

[b]2. To expand on everything you loved about the game and make the world even more immersive. [/b]
The idea would be to add more world events, more living world (roaming traders, roaming beasts), 
to expand on the housing, war, crime and on the mercenary systems. 
The expansion would also bring a new island-like area to explore.

If there is something else you would really love to see being a part of an expansion, 
feel free to suggest it over Discord or Steam forums, and we will take it into consideration.

If the game continues to receive love and support, as it has so far, expect more info about the expansion in the second part of next year.

notes.title: Game Design Choices
notes.notes:
Here are the core principles we used to create this game:

[b]1. Freedom of Actions[/b]
We will throw you into an open world and start the main quest. 
Besides that, it is up to you to decide what you will do. 
Yes, you can go from the start to find one of the final bosses in the game and try to fight them, we will not stop you. 
When it comes to the story, you will have the chance to pick sides and end the game in different ways.

[b]2. Consequences[/b]
We introduce consequences through the death mechanic, world events, the story, and sometimes even dialogues. 
We do this to keep you invested in the world. 
The higher the stakes, the more you will be invested in the game, and the more you will care. 
For this reason, we highly recommend leaving Ironman mode enabled. 
That being said, consequences should never feel frustrating. 
If you get stuck somewhere, the game should start helping you in various ways. 
We are in this experience together. We closely follow player feedback, and we will loosen up consequences in places where players have issues with the game. 
The whole experience should be and stay fun in the first place.

[b]3. Player versus Developer Approach[/b]
We grew up playing and loving games such as Gothic. 
What we loved the most in those games was trying to abuse the freedom we received to break the game. 
For example, I would spend half an hour kiting the late-game bear to get its loot, and it felt so satisfying when I finally managed to do that.
In Svarog's Dream, your job is to try to outsmart us by using given mechanics, and our job is to lay traps for you. 

[previewyoutube=m-oquDWJThs;righthumb][/previewyoutube] With time invested, you will eventually win, but we will surprise you many times when we predict your moves, and the fun lies in this whole interaction between you and us. 
Here, we captured one moment on stream of a new player experiencing the game as we imagined it.
We spent so much time working on small details, and you will often be surprised by twists like this when they happen to you.


[b]4. Freedom of Interpretation[/b]
We imagined a few different interpretations of the game and then went through the game over and over to support them all. 
The game should be for you what you decide it is.
This whole project was personal for me (Ivan), as it took four years of my life to finish it. 
During that period, I read a lot of (Eastern and European) philosophy and went through a process of rediscovery, 
so some of the in-game quests may reflect that.
Here are some interpretations we wanted to support:
Ending 3: 
[spoiler]You are in this fight to help the light side win against the dark side and save the fantasy world.[/spoiler]
Ending 2: 
[spoiler]Old Gods represent ego, the new god represents presence (the eye behind the ego), the world is experience, and you as a player are free will.[/spoiler]
Ending 4: 
[spoiler]You are Svarog, the God Creator.
While playing the game, you are in a state of sleep, and the whole goal is to wake up, leave the sleep, and start looking around yourself.[/spoiler]
We tried to support few more interpretations, but in the end, the game can be whatever you decide it is, and you are the only one to decide that.

What do you think about those? Are you experiencing what we intended to create? Feel free to leave comments below.

Best regards, Ivan Ristic.

notes.title: It took us 4 years to get here.
notes.notes:
We are so close to the release of Svarog's Dream and in this article, we will share some insights into the path that led us here.

The idea of making a video game was born a decade ago, but it all seriously began when I was playing EU4, the strategy game, somewhere in 2019.
The game immersed me so much that every decision had consequences, yet none of them felt unfair. You felt like you were part of something bigger.

Back then, I wondered why there weren't more RPGs like that.
I had also played Kenshi, and seeing Chris Hunt create such a masterpiece almost solo made me think,
why couldn't I start working on the game I wanted to see?

For the next six months, using just pen and paper I worked on the design of this RPG alone.
Aiming to make the world feel alive, similar to EU4, I added world events. 
In order to introduce consequences to the game, I designed some mechanics to support this, such as the unique death system this game has.

At the same time, I read a lot of fantasy books, and it struck me what the story should be.
The world and story should be set in the fantasy realm of Slavic mythology.
While Greek and Nordic mythologies are fantastic, what I love about Slavic mythology is that original sources are mixed and unclear, leaving a lot of room for fantasy and imagination to fill these missing parts. The Witcher series showed us in the past how fantasy mixed with Slavic mythology can work great. 
Besides, Slavic mythology has always been close to my heart.
This background was perfect for shaping the game's narrative. Months were dedicated to crafting the story and quests.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/yJqpnjx.png[/img]
 
Finally, around 2020, I began solo work on the MVP, which was completed after six months of effort.
After that, my wife joined in assisting with the art and other aspects outside the game.
We then hired a few contractors within our budget, selected assets and implemented them, gradually starting to invite people to test early builds.

The closed beta of the game started two years ago, when the game was only 30% complete.
We invited a select few to provide feedback.
Over the next two years, we worked intensely on the game, with the goal of bringing the experience we imagined while also working with those who joined us, constantly refining the Svarog’s Dream.

With the Steam Festival demo, another group of people who liked the game joined the beta, aiding us in noticing, fixing and polishing many small details the game needed.

The list of people who helped with feedback is huge. You can find those who were the most dedicated in the game credits, under a special QA section. There are about 20 names there, and we appreciate all of them for helping us shape Svarog’s Dream.

After nine months of work on design and narrative and over 40 months of development, we find ourselves at the finish line.
The game will be released in four days.
What happens after that? Stay with us and follow our story.

Ivan Ristic, Lead Developer.

Throughout the 7 days of Steam Next Fest, while the demo is active, you can explore our game and try to find 21 out of the 25 dream flowers hidden in the world.

If you manage to do this, send us a screenshot and provide feedback about the game so that we can make it even better. This way, we will know you explored the demo thoroughly, and we will appreciate your feedback even more.

You will also [b]secure your place in the game credits[/b] under the "Special Thanks" section.

At the end of the week, we will release a video revealing the locations of all the dream flowers and other hidden secrets within the demo. After that, the demo will conclude.

After the video revealing the secrets, we will rebroadcast our first video showcasing the demo gameplay, commented on by developers. Developers will be present in the chat to answer all your questions, so stick with us if you missed it earlier. Or simply if you wish to chat with us.


[img]https://i.imgur.com/IIHMm1k.png[/img]

Svarog's Dream is coming—arise, arise!

notes.title: Svarog's Dream Demo: Gameplay with Developers
notes.notes:
After four years of development, "Svarog's Dream," the open-world RPG, is finally here! 
Join us during the Steam Next Festival for two exciting live broadcasts. 
The first showcases our demo gameplay while developers are commenting on it.

Our developers will be on hand to answer all your questions through the chat. Don't miss it!
